---
description: Web development standards for code generated by framework agents. These rules apply to the actual application code produced, not to the framework itself.
---

# Web Development Instructions

This file defines coding standards for **generated code** from framework agents. These are the rules agents follow when creating React components, APIs, tests, etc.

## Tech Stack Standards

### Frontend Requirements
- **Framework**: React 18+ with TypeScript
- **Styling**: TailwindCSS or CSS Modules (separate files)
- **State**: Zustand, React Context, or Redux Toolkit
- **Routing**: React Router v6
- **Forms**: React Hook Form + Zod validation
- **HTTP**: Fetch API or Axios
- **Build**: Vite

### Backend Requirements (if applicable)
- **Runtime**: Node.js with Express or Next.js API Routes
- **Database**: PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM
- **Auth**: JWT or session-based
- **API**: RESTful or GraphQL

### Testing Requirements
- **Unit**: Vitest
- **Component**: React Testing Library
- **E2E**: Playwright
- **Coverage**: Minimum 80% for critical paths

## TypeScript Standards

### Strict Mode Required
```json
// tsconfig.json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "noImplicitAny": true,
    "strictNullChecks": true
  }
}
```

### Type Definitions
- ✅ Explicit types for all function parameters
- ✅ Explicit return types for all functions
- ✅ Interfaces for object shapes
- ✅ Type aliases for unions/intersections
- ✅ Generics for reusable components
- ❌ No `any` type (use `unknown` or specific types)
- ❌ No type assertions unless absolutely necessary

### Example
```typescript
// ✅ GOOD
interface UserProps {
  name: string;
  age: number;
  email?: string;
}

function getUser(id: number): Promise<UserProps> {
  return fetch(`/api/users/${id}`).then(res => res.json());
}

// ❌ BAD
function getUser(id: any): any {
  return fetch(`/api/users/${id}`).then(res => res.json());
}
```

## React Standards

### Component Rules
- ✅ Functional components only (no class components)
- ✅ Named exports (no default exports)
- ✅ TypeScript interfaces for props
- ✅ Destructure props in function signature
- ✅ Default values for optional props
- ❌ No React.FC or React.FunctionComponent type
- ❌ No prop spreading unless necessary
- ❌ No index as key in lists

### Example
```typescript
// ✅ GOOD
interface ButtonProps {
  label: string;
  onClick: () => void;
  variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary';
  disabled?: boolean;
}

export function Button({
  label,
  onClick,
  variant = 'primary',
  disabled = false
}: ButtonProps) {
  return (
    <button
      onClick={onClick}
      disabled={disabled}
      className={styles[variant]}
    >
      {label}
    </button>
  );
}

// ❌ BAD
export default function Button(props: any) {
  return <button {...props}>{props.label}</button>;
}
```

### Hooks Guidelines
- ✅ `useState` for local state
- ✅ `useEffect` with cleanup function when needed
- ✅ `useCallback` only when passing to memoized children
- ✅ `useMemo` only when expensive computation
- ✅ Custom hooks start with "use" prefix
- ❌ No useEffect without dependency array
- ❌ No unnecessary optimization (measure first)

### Conditional Rendering
Prefer early returns over nested ternaries:

```typescript
// ✅ GOOD
export function UserProfile({ userId }: Props) {
  if (!userId) return <div>No user selected</div>;
  if (loading) return <Spinner />;
  if (error) return <ErrorMessage error={error} />;
  return <UserDetails user={user} />;
}

// ❌ BAD
export function UserProfile({ userId }: Props) {
  return userId ? (loading ? <Spinner /> : (error ? <ErrorMessage error={error} /> : <UserDetails user={user} />)) : <div>No user selected</div>;
}
```

## File Organization

### Project Structure
```
src/
├── components/          # Reusable UI components
│   ├── Button/
│   │   ├── Button.tsx
│   │   ├── Button.test.tsx
│   │   └── Button.module.css
│   └── ...
├── pages/              # Page-level components
├── features/           # Feature-based modules
├── hooks/              # Custom React hooks
├── services/           # API calls and external services
├── utils/              # Helper functions
├── types/              # Shared TypeScript types
├── constants/          # App-wide constants
└── assets/             # Static assets (images, icons)
```

### Naming Conventions
- **Components**: PascalCase (`Button.tsx`, `UserProfile.tsx`)
- **Hooks**: camelCase with "use" prefix (`useAuth.ts`, `useFetch.ts`)
- **Utils**: camelCase (`formatDate.ts`, `validateEmail.ts`)
- **Constants**: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (`API_BASE_URL`, `MAX_FILE_SIZE`)
- **Types**: PascalCase (`User`, `ApiResponse`)
- **CSS Modules**: camelCase (`styles.container`, `styles.primaryButton`)

## Code Style

### Formatting Rules
- **Indentation**: 2 spaces (no tabs)
- **Quotes**: Single quotes for strings, double quotes for JSX attributes
- **Semicolons**: Always required
- **Line Length**: Maximum 100 characters
- **Trailing Commas**: Yes for multi-line arrays/objects
- **Arrow Functions**: Preferred for all functions

### Example
```typescript
// ✅ GOOD
const users = [
  { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
  { id: 2, name: 'Bob' },
];

const getUserName = (user: User): string => {
  return user.name;
};

// ❌ BAD
const users = [
    { id: 1, name: "Alice" },
    { id: 2, name: "Bob" }
]

function getUserName(user: User): string
{
  return user.name
}
```

## Accessibility (A11y)

### Requirements
- ✅ Semantic HTML (header, nav, main, article, section, footer)
- ✅ Alt text for all images
- ✅ Keyboard navigation support (Tab, Enter, Esc)
- ✅ ARIA labels only when semantic HTML insufficient
- ✅ Color contrast WCAG AA (4.5:1 for text)
- ✅ Visible focus indicators
- ✅ Screen reader testing (VoiceOver/NVDA)

### Example
```typescript
// ✅ GOOD
<button
  onClick={handleClick}
  aria-label="Close dialog"
>
  <CloseIcon />
</button>

<img
  src="/avatar.jpg"
  alt="User profile photo of John Doe"
/>

// ❌ BAD
<div onClick={handleClick}>  {/* Not keyboard accessible */}
  <span>×</span>
</div>

<img src="/avatar.jpg" />  {/* Missing alt */}
```

## Performance

### Optimization Requirements
- ✅ Code splitting with `React.lazy()` and `Suspense`
- ✅ Image optimization (WebP, responsive, lazy loading)
- ✅ Bundle size monitoring (`vite-bundle-visualizer`)
- ✅ List virtualization for long lists (`react-virtual`)
- ✅ Debouncing/throttling for event handlers
- ✅ Core Web Vitals: LCP < 2.5s, FID < 100ms, CLS < 0.1

### Example
```typescript
// ✅ GOOD - Code splitting
const AdminPanel = lazy(() => import('./AdminPanel'));

function App() {
  return (
    <Suspense fallback={<Spinner />}>
      <AdminPanel />
    </Suspense>
  );
}

// ✅ GOOD - Debouncing
import { debounce } from 'lodash-es';

const handleSearch = debounce((query: string) => {
  fetchResults(query);
}, 300);
```

## Security

### Security Requirements
- ✅ Validate all inputs (frontend + backend)
- ✅ Sanitize user content before rendering (XSS prevention)
- ✅ HTTPS for all API calls
- ✅ CORS properly configured
- ✅ HttpOnly cookies for tokens
- ✅ Environment variables for secrets (never hardcode)
- ✅ Rate limiting for sensitive endpoints
- ✅ Content Security Policy (CSP) headers

### Example
```typescript
// ✅ GOOD - Input validation
import { z } from 'zod';

const userSchema = z.object({
  email: z.string().email(),
  age: z.number().min(0).max(120),
});

function createUser(data: unknown) {
  const validated = userSchema.parse(data); // Throws if invalid
  return api.post('/users', validated);
}

// ❌ BAD - No validation
function createUser(data: any) {
  return api.post('/users', data);
}
```

## Error Handling

### Requirements
- ✅ Try-catch for all async operations
- ✅ User-friendly error messages (no stack traces)
- ✅ Log errors with context (user ID, timestamp, action)
- ✅ Error boundaries for React components
- ✅ Toast notifications for user feedback
- ✅ Retry logic for failed API calls

### Example
```typescript
// ✅ GOOD
async function fetchUser(id: number): Promise<User> {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/users/${id}`);
    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(`Failed to fetch user: ${response.statusText}`);
    }
    return await response.json();
  } catch (error) {
    logger.error('User fetch failed', { id, error });
    throw new Error('Unable to load user. Please try again.');
  }
}

// ❌ BAD
async function fetchUser(id: number) {
  const response = await fetch(`/api/users/${id}`);
  return response.json();
}
```

## Testing Philosophy

### Testing Principles
- ✅ Test user behavior, not implementation details
- ✅ Write tests before or during development (TDD encouraged)
- ✅ Mock external dependencies (APIs, browser APIs)
- ✅ Test error cases and edge cases
- ✅ Use test IDs, not CSS selectors
- ✅ Write descriptive test names

### Example
```typescript
// ✅ GOOD
import { render, screen, userEvent } from '@testing-library/react';
import { Button } from './Button';

describe('Button', () => {
  it('calls onClick handler when clicked', async () => {
    const handleClick = vi.fn();
    render(<Button label="Click me" onClick={handleClick} />);

    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Click me' }));

    expect(handleClick).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  it('is disabled when disabled prop is true', () => {
    render(<Button label="Click me" onClick={vi.fn()} disabled />);

    expect(screen.getByRole('button')).toBeDisabled();
  });
});

// ❌ BAD
it('test1', () => {
  const wrapper = mount(<Button />);
  wrapper.find('.button').simulate('click');
  expect(wrapper.state().clicked).toBe(true);
});
```

## Git Workflow

### Commit Message Format
Follow Conventional Commits:
```
feat: add user authentication
fix: resolve button alignment issue
docs: update README with setup instructions
style: format code with prettier
refactor: extract API logic into service layer
test: add tests for user registration
chore: update dependencies
perf: improve list rendering performance
```

### Branch Naming
- `feature/user-authentication`
- `bugfix/header-overflow`
- `hotfix/security-vulnerability`
- `refactor/api-service-layer`

## API Integration

### API Standards
- ✅ Environment variables for API URLs
- ✅ Loading states for all async operations
- ✅ Error states with retry option
- ✅ Request/response interceptors for auth headers
- ✅ Request caching where appropriate
- ✅ Optimistic updates for better UX
- ✅ Pagination for large datasets

### Example
```typescript
// ✅ GOOD
const API_BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL;

interface ApiResponse<T> {
  data: T;
  error?: string;
  loading: boolean;
}

async function fetchUsers(): Promise<User[]> {
  const response = await fetch(`${API_BASE_URL}/users`, {
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${getToken()}`,
    },
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error('Failed to fetch users');
  }

  return response.json();
}
```

## Anti-Patterns (Don'ts)

### Forbidden Practices
- ❌ No `any` types without excellent reason
- ❌ No `console.log` in production code
- ❌ No inline styles (except dynamic values)
- ❌ No functions longer than 50 lines
- ❌ No deeply nested ternary operators
- ❌ No mutation of props or state
- ❌ No unnecessary re-renders (check useEffect dependencies)
- ❌ No commits without tests
- ❌ No hardcoded URLs or credentials
- ❌ No inline `<style>` or `<script>` tags in HTML

## Quick Reference Commands

```bash
# Development

pnpm build            # Build for production
pnpm preview          # Preview production build

# Testing
pnpm test             # Run unit tests
pnpm test:watch       # Run tests in watch mode
pnpm test:coverage    # Generate coverage report
pnpm test:e2e         # Run E2E tests

# Code Quality
pnpm lint             # Run ESLint
pnpm lint:fix         # Fix ESLint issues
pnpm format           # Format with Prettier
pnpm type-check       # TypeScript type checking
```
